requirements.requirement: The system must compute a raw proximity score for each clinical trial using both distance (miles) and duration (minutes) returned from Google Routes.
The system must apply an inverse relationship such that lower distance and shorter duration produce higher raw proximity scores.
The system must combine distance and duration into a single score using a deterministic weighted function.
The system must ensure the weighting function produces consistent outputs for identical inputs across executions.
The system must normalize all raw proximity scores within a result set to a 0–100 scale.
The system must ensure the highest proximity (closest/fastest) trial in a result set receives a normalized score of 100.
The system must ensure the lowest proximity (farthest/slowest) trial in a result set receives a normalized score of 0 or the minimum defined baseline.
The system must handle multiple trials in a single computation batch and normalize scores relative only to that batch.
The system must produce identical normalized scores regardless of input order of trials.
The system must include both distance and duration values used in scoring alongside the computed score for traceability.
The system must handle zero-distance cases by assigning the maximum possible proximity score before normalization.
The system must cap extreme outlier distances or durations to prevent distortion of normalization across the result set.
The system must return a null or explicitly flagged proximity score when distance or duration data is missing from Google Routes.
The system must exclude trials with missing proximity inputs from normalization calculations while still returning them in the response.
The system must log scoring inputs and outputs for each trial to support auditability and debugging.
The system must execute proximity scoring without invoking any non-deterministic or LLM-based components.
The system must ensure scoring logic is implemented as a reusable function within clinical_trials_service.
The system must complete proximity score computation for a standard result set (<=50 trials) within acceptable backend latency thresholds.
